newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ASX GIVES AMP OKAY TO SEEK SHAREHOLDER LIMIT RULE.
newsitem.headline: ASX GIVES AMP OKAY TO SEEK SHAREHOLDER LIMIT RULE.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange said on Thursday it has given in-principle agreement to a request by the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) that its policyholders be asked to approve a shareholder limitation clause.
AMP, Australia's largest insurance and funds manager, wants a five percent shareholding limit for five years from the date of listing included in its articles of association.
The ASX said the proposal would be described in an exploratory memorandum and would be considered by policyholders at a meeting later this year.
AMP plans to demutualise and list on the ASX sometime in 1998.
The ASX said it had approved shareholder limits of 10 percent for a five year period in the case of Colonial Ltd and Australian Pharmaceutical Industies Ltd.
It said the position is consistent with the approach taken in the United Kingdom and the United States when mutuals and coooperatives sought a sharemarket listing.
The state government of New South Wales recently passed legislation which granted AMP a five percent shareholder limit for up to two years.
"ASX is conscious that more than one million AMP policyholders may become shareholders of the demutualised entity," ASX managing director Richard Humphry said.

"It is reasonable for ASX to allow a transitionary period during which these shareholders, many of them first-time investors in the sharemarket, can become apprised of what it really means to be a shareholder, their rights, obligations and the information that is available to them to make an informed decision about their investment," he said.

AMP, which has funds under management of more than A$100 billion and annual net profits of about A$2.0 billion, will become one of the nation's top 10 listed companies when it joins the exchange boards, analysts have said.
The company would have a large and open share register as well, they said.
